archetypes.name: surface-sweep
archetypes.rationale: The plan targets a specific file list, but complete --simple removal requires verifying no stale references exist outside that list across the entire live surface.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every file in the repo (excluding larch-logs/, .git/, and CHANGELOG.md) for the literal string '--simple' and compare each hit against the plan's listed files to determine whether the plan's modification set is complete. For each hit outside the plan's file list, classify it as: a live-surface reference requiring a new edit, a test fixture that needs updating, or benign archived content the plan correctly excludes. Pay special attention to hooks/, scripts/, agents/, and .claude-plugin/ paths that carry runtime surface. Verify the plan's post-implementation completeness gate claim that a grep over *.md/*.sh/*.json/*.txt/*.tsv/*.toml returns zero rows. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: outcome-enum-audit
archetypes.rationale: The plan retires cancelled-tier-gate on a sole-producer claim; any missed emitter or consumer breaks the renderer or leaves a dead enum value that diverges the SKILL enum from the script allow-list.
archetypes.prompt_body: Grep for the exact string 'cancelled-tier-gate' across all files and verify it appears only in the four retirement targets the plan identifies: the SKILL.md SUMMARY_OUTCOME enum, the render-final-summary.sh case branch, the test-render-final-summary.sh test loop, and the render-run-summary.md outcomes table. For each additional hit, classify it as a producer (emits the outcome string), a consumer (routes on it), or documentation the plan should have updated. Cross-check whether any other SUMMARY_OUTCOME enum values in SKILL.md are similarly only in the renderer case branch or also appear in scripts that produce them, to confirm the retirement approach is internally consistent. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
